sourceNote: Adversarial case testing cognitive trap: anchoring bias on growth metrics while missing retention issues.

ownerIntake.businessType: Team collaboration SaaS platform, competing with Slack/Teams
ownerIntake.stage: ARR $12M, 50% YoY growth, 45k active accounts, churn 4% MRR
ownerConstraints: Pressure to demonstrate growth for Series C
ownerIntake.immediateConcern: Impressive growth rate (50% YoY) creating overconfidence about product-market fit, but churn is rising (was 2% MoM 12 months ago, now 4% MoM). Trap: leadership focused on growth metric, blind to deteriorating retention.
availableData: ARR $12M, growth 50% YoY, 45k accounts, churn 4% MoM

businessProblem: SaaS company celebrating 50% growth rate but ignoring doubling of churn rate (2%→4% MoM), embedding overconfidence about product-market fit when retention signals suggest otherwise. Trap: growth metric anchoring masks retention deterioration.

evidence.finding: ARR growing 50% YoY from $8M to $12M (impressive). Churn rising from 2% MoM (12 mo ago) to 4% MoM (current), a 100% increase in churn rate.
